prompt: Generate an SQL INSERT statement from any object by reading its @Table and @Column annotations with reflection. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Annotations on a class and on its fields carry the mapping between Java names and database names, so one generic builder replaces a hand-written INSERT per table. getAnnotation on the Class object reads the type-level @Table, while the same call on each Field reads @Column -- both return null rather than throwing when the marker is absent. Building the column list and the value list in the same loop keeps them aligned, which is the one thing an INSERT cannot get wrong. Quoting only String values is a deliberate simplification: a real mapper would use a prepared statement instead, because string concatenation invites SQL injection.
hints: row.getClass().getAnnotation(Table.class) gives you the table name via table.name(); check for null before using it.
Use two StringBuilders and append ", " to both only when they are not empty yet -- that keeps the separators right without a trailing comma.
Write a small private helper that formats one value: null becomes NULL, a String gets single quotes around it, anything else goes through String.valueOf.
